conservation.condition_narrative:
1. The dark purple-brown paint scuff was reduced as much as possible using tiny swabs with acetone. Orange paint scuffs in the bottom right corner were removed in the same way with petroleum benzine. 
2. The remaining bits of purple-brown paint and small losses from the gouge in the bottom right corner were inpainted using dry pigments mixed in MS2A with Stoddards solvent. 
All the work was done under the stereomicroscope. 
The treatment was documented with color slides. 
Conservator: Besty Court 
Conservation Technician: Erick Gude 
Dates of Treatment: November 30 and December 1, 2004 
MS2A: modified polycyclohexanone reduced ketone resin (Linden Nazareth, U.K.)

description: This painting has *Untitled (Abstraction)*, 1919 (cat. no. 308) on the back side of the canvas.  Two dark green, tree trunk-like shapes diverge from one another, creating a V-shape within the composition. Between the two trunks, a white maple leaf floats against a greenish-brown background.
